title: Gesture-led client contracts and deferred toolplay (PRD draft)
summary: Draft proposal for a lightweight, gesture-oriented client contract for the Hosted API that enables progressive streaming, declarative tool invocation, and deferred toolplay (postponed or conditional tool execution). Emphasis is on SDK ergonomics: small, composable client gestures that make it easy to express intent, cancelation, and resume while preserving structured output guarantees and observability.
problem_statement: Teams integrating tool-calling and structured streaming into clients face tradeoffs: either the client must manage complex event choreography and retries, or the server exposes a heavyweight protocol that’s brittle across SDKs and languages. Current streaming contracts conflate partial text frames with tool semantics, leading to fragile client-side heuristics and duplicated retry logic.
goals: Define a minimal set of client gestures (start, checkpoint, defer, commit, cancel, replay) that cover common interactive flows without exposing internal runtime complexity.
Specify a streaming frame format that cleanly separates narrative tokens from structured tool events and deferred tool intents.
Design SDK primitives that are idiomatic in JS/Python/Go: promise-friendly, cancellable, and easy to compose with UI frameworks.
Provide server-side semantics for deferred toolplay so tool invocations can be resolved later, retried, or executed conditionally based on user confirmation or additional context.
Maintain observability hooks: per-gesture tracing, idempotency keys, and token-level cost attributions for deferred actions.
Enable graceful degradation: if deferred tool execution is not supported in a deployment, clients can fall back to immediate tool calls with clear semantics.
non_goals: Full replacement of existing streaming protocol in a single rollout — this is an incremental pattern that should interoperate with current endpoints.
Opinionating on UI-level confirmation UX beyond basic examples; we provide primitives, not design-system components.
Implementing a distributed scheduler for deferred tasks in this PRD — backend scheduling will remain an implementation detail for Dedicated/Private deployments.
user_stories: As a chat UI developer, I want to show partial assistant text while the assistant declares a tool intent (e.g., 'suggestCalendarEvent') so users can read and accept before the tool runs.
As a product engineer, I want to defer a high-cost external call (billing query) until the user approves a summary, so we reduce unnecessary cost and improve perceived latency.
As an SDK user, I want a single cancellable handle that covers streaming text + tool invocation, so I can wire it to a cancel button with minimal glue code.
As an SRE, I want idempotency and clear tracing for deferred tool executions so we can reconcile partial failures and reruns safely.
As a solutions engineer, I want the API to clearly indicate deployments that support deferred toolplay so I can configure fallbacks for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: Protocol spec: canonical streaming frame with separate fields for narrative tokens, tool-intent frames, and deferred-action markers, with JSON examples for each.
SDK surfaces defined for JS and Python: startGesture(), onCheckpoint(), deferTool(), commitDeferred(), cancelGesture(), replayGesture(handle).
Backward compatibility: clients can opt-in; existing clients continue to work without changes and can detect server capability via capability handshake header.
Integration tests demonstrating: partial text + deferred tool intent, user-confirmed commit executing the tool, server-side retry with idempotency key, and offline resume of deferred actions.
Telemetry schema: per-gesture id, start/commit/cancel timestamps, token counts, tool execution latency, and cost attribution tags.
Migration guide draft for SDK authors and docs team.
requirements: Protocol: include a 'gesture_id' at the session and message level to correlate frames.
Frame types: 'text_chunk', 'tool_intent', 'deferred_marker', 'checkpoint', 'error'. Each frame must be individually parseable so thin clients can render progressively.
Tool intent schema: {tool_name, args_schema_version, preview_payload}. Preview payload must be small (<4KB) and safe for untrusted rendering.
Deferred action lifecycle: created -> pending -> committed -> executed -> acknowledged. Server must return status updates as frames.
Idempotency: client-supplied idempotency keys for deferred executions; server honors and surfaces collisions.
Capability discovery: HTTP header X-HostedAPI-Features or handshake response listing 'deferred_toolplay', 'gesture_contract_v1'.
SDK ergonomics: abortable Promises/async-iterators in JS; context-managers and generator-style iterators in Python; clear cancellation semantics in Go.
Security: preview_payload must be sanitized; deferred tool execution must enforce RBAC and KMS token scoping for enterprise/private deployments.
Observability: tracing spans per gesture, and logs for deferred state transitions with searchable fields.
Fallbacks: server must support an immediate-execute fallback when client requests deferred and backend does not allow it, responding with explicit status frame.
api_surface_notes: New optional endpoint parameter: ?gesture_mode=on which toggles gesture framing for the session.
Streaming response schema example included in body. Consumers that do not parse frames should continue to receive a concatenated text stream under a compatibility path.

Client-to-server control messages (for commit/cancel) are sent over a control websocket or a companion REST endpoint /gestures/{gesture_id}/control. The companion REST path is recommended for short-lived environments and better cross-language parity.
Error semantics: transient errors (network, capacity) should produce checkpoint frames the client can resume from; terminal errors must include a machine-readable code and human-friendly message.
Quota & billing: deferred tool executions are charged at execution time; preview frames incur normal token billing.
sdk_ergonomics: - for await (const frame of handle.stream()) { render(frame); if (frame.type === 'tool_intent') showPreview(frame.preview); }
- handle.cancel(); // cancels ongoing stream and any pending deferred actions on client side
- Keep gesture handles small and instance-bound (not global).
- Minimize async surface: stream + a couple of imperative helpers (defer/commit/cancel/replay).
- Provide first-class rehydration: gesture metadata must be persistable for resume across reloads (small JSON).
- Avoid exposing internal sequence numbers to SDK users; use opaque gesture_id and frame cursors.
streaming_contract_examples: Thin clients can ignore frames they don't understand and render concatenated text from text_chunk frames.
tool_calling_semantics: Deferred vs immediate: clients can request tool invocation with 'execute_now' or 'defer'. 'defer' returns a deferred_id and does not trigger backend action until committed.
Previews: tool_intent frames should include a small preview and an optional UI-safe HTML snippet; servers must strip dangerous content.
Conditional execution: commitDeferred call can include updated args (to support user edits) and a client-supplied confirmation token.
Retries: server retries use idempotency keys. If a deferred action fails, server emits a 'deferred_error' frame with retryable flag and suggested backoff.
Visibility & control: admins can query /gestures/{gesture_id}/deferred to list pending deferred actions for auditing.
structured_output_schema: We propose a lightweight JSON-LD-ish envelope for structured outputs that coexists with text frames:
- tool_intent.body uses a declared schema reference: schema://calendar/v1/create
- previews use a 'safe_preview' subfield (text + denormalized attributes) and an optional 'render_hint' string for clients.
- When a tool executes, server returns an 'execution_result' frame with a link to auditable artifacts (s3:// or internal artifact id) and a minimal success/failure payload.
- Schema versioning: include a schema_version on each tool frame for forward/backward compatibility.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (internal e2e) — 3 weeks: implement prototype server framing + SDK experiment in JS, run internal playtests with solutions-team scenarios.
Phase 1 (beta customers) — 6 weeks: opt-in capability flag, SDK docs, two pilot customers (chat + automation) on hosted and dedicated deployments.
Phase 2 (general availability) — 4 weeks: expand SDKs (Python/Go), add telemetry dashboards, finalize billing model for deferred executions.
Phase 3 (enterprise readiness) — ongoing: hardened RBAC, KMS integration for tool credentials, and ability to persist deferred actions to customer-managed stores for Private deployments.
metrics: Adoption: % of new streaming sessions created with gesture_mode=on
User flow: % deferred actions committed vs canceled
Cost: average backend charge per deferred action vs immediate executes
Latency: time from commitDeferred -> execution start
Reliability: deferred execution success rate and retry counts
Observability: % of gestures with full trace spans captured
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Deferred actions increase backend complexity and storage needs. Mitigation: limit default TTL to 24 hours and require explicit opt-in for long-retention in enterprise plans.
Risk: Security exposure through previews. Mitigation: sanitize previews and mark untrusted content; enterprise customers can opt-out of previews.
Risk: Developer confusion over gesture vs non-gesture clients. Mitigation: clear capability handshake, compatibility mode that returns plain text when client lacks support.
Risk: Billing surprises if customers commit many deferred actions. Mitigation: surface cost estimate in preview frames and in console before commit.
open_questions: Do we require server-side persistence for all deferred actions or allow ephemeral deferred state only for hosted ephemeral sessions?
Should preview frames be automatically cached by the platform to avoid recomputation on commit?
How do we expose audit logs for deferred actions in Private deployments without leaking internal artifacts?
What is the canonical backoff/retry policy for deferred executions that fail transiently?
next_steps: Align with runtime team on gesture_id propagation across routing and fallback to synchronous variants (owner: Noah Kim).
Prototype JS SDK handle and internal QA playbook (owner: Maya Rodriguez).
Design console telemetry surfaces and billing preview UI with product-marketing (owner: Liam Patel).
Schedule an API review and security threat model for previews and deferred execution (owner: Ava Chen).
body:
Context and motivation:

This draft explores a middle path between verbose control-plane protocols and brittle client-side heuristics. We want a compact gesture contract that: 1) lets clients render progressive text, 2) surfaces tool intents in a safe preview, and 3) defers execution until an explicit commit. The pattern aims to reduce wasted backend work, improve perceived latency, and provide clearer contract boundaries for SDKs.

Implementation notes and experiments to run:

- Experiment A: JS host with optimistic preview + commit flow connected to a stubbed calendar tool. Measure commit latency and UX timing profiles.
- Experiment B: Python SDK with persisted gesture metadata that survives page reload (store small JSON in client local storage). Validate idempotency on commit.
- Experiment C: Server-side resource limiter for pending deferred queue to validate TTL and auto-cancel behavior.

Docs and developer guidance (annex):

- Migration snippet for existing streaming clients showing compatibility path.
- Example UI patterns: in-line preview card with accept/edit/decline buttons wired to defer/commit/cancel API.
- Troubleshooting checklist: common failures, how to inspect gesture traces in console, how to reconcile missing deferred actions.

We invite feedback from SDK leads, runtime, security, and solutions engineering. The intention is to keep the surface area small and iterate quickly with two pilot customers before wider rollout.
